extracted.intended_audience: individuals, community advocates, and organizations (U.S.) who want to submit public comments on federal rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for finding open federal rulemakings and preparing and submitting public comments (via regulations.gov or Federal Register) during the official notice-and-comment period. Covers who may submit, what to include, deadlines, and submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding open regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Search two primary sources: Regulations.gov (official submission portal) and Federalregister.gov (daily publication with email alerts). Filter by agency, docket number, or posting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Regulations.gov to locate the docket where you can submit comments and FederalRegister.gov to track new publications and set up email alerts. Narrow searches by agency name, docket number, or posting date to find the specific rulemaking you want to comment on. Check the docket for supplementary materials and related documents before drafting your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission timeline and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit comments any time during the comment period, which is usually 30 or 60 days from the date that the regulation is published. Comments must arrive before midnight Eastern Time on the specified deadline date—the portal closes at that exact time regardless of your local timezone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the exact comment period in the Federal Register notice and submit early (do not wait until the last day). Note the deadline timezone (midnight ET) and plan accordingly. Late submissions generally will not be reviewed, so allow buffer time for technical issues or mail delivery if submitting by post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can submit and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may participate anonymously or representing an organization. No specialized credentials required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals, community members, advocates, and organizations can all file comments. You may submit anonymously if desired, or identify yourself/your organization if you want the agency to have contact information or to show organizational support. There is no requirement for professional credentials to submit a comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to include in comments (content guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: What to include: Personal impacts on you, family, or community; Data and survey results; Stories from affected community members; Any relevant information for agency consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine personal narrative with concrete evidence where possible—describe specific harms or benefits, provide data, cite surveys or studies, and include names/locations/timelines when appropriate. Use stories from affected community members to illustrate impacts. Aim to give the agency information that directly informs the agency's consideration of the rule (e.g., costs, operational impacts, logistical constraints). Avoid vague, unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies only must consider comments directly relevant to the specific regulation. Off-topic submissions and late comments won't be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each point ties to the rule or specific regulatory text or question in the notice; reference docket numbers, proposed regulatory sections, or specific provisions you address. Do not use the docket to raise unrelated policy grievances. If you want the agency to adopt a change, clearly explain the requested change and the rationale/evidence supporting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods, format, and language
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission (in English) via regulations.gov or Federal Register is standard. Follow specific instructions provided—some rules require mailing instead. You may type content directly or upload a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via the portal indicated in the Federal Register notice (typically Regulations.gov). If the notice allows attachments, follow the agency's file-type, size, and formatting rules; if the notice requires mailed comments, follow the mailing instructions exactly. Always follow any docket-specific submission instructions, include the docket number or agency identifier, and submit in English unless the agency provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies' legal obligation to consider comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must legally review and consider public submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that agencies are required to review and consider timely, relevant comments as part of the administrative record for a rulemaking. This does not guarantee a particular outcome, but well-documented, relevant comments can influence agency decisionmaking and the final rule. Keep records of your submission confirmation for future reference.
